mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 3% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth < -2% AND HOUST falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for four consecutive months, combined with accelerating average hourly earnings growth (proxied by INDPRO > 0.4% monthly), signals labor market overheating and impending wage-price pressure, which increases recession risk and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for four consecutive months AND INDPRO > 0.4% in the last month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month contraction in industrial production (INDPRO < 0% for two consecutive months) indicates supply-side weakness, which reduces corporate revenue growth and compresses profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is in contraction for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession (UNRATE > 5%) signals aggressive monetary easing, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS growth > 2%) alongside a simultaneous decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (GDPC1 < 0% YoY change) signals a precautionary savings shift, which reduces near-term consumption and corporate sales, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 2% AND GDPC1 YoY growth < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS > 0.5% month-over-month) for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO > 0.5% for four consecutive months) signals improving supply capacity and corporate output, which raises earnings expectations and yields positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
